implementerProof.how: Round four answers the second review round (changes requested at c0cacf98: the branch conflicting with main, and five minors). Since round three the branch has two forward merges (55e8991d, which renumbers this change's Dispatch migration 0148_dpop_proofs to 0149_dpop_proofs because main took 0148, and b5103ea3, one text conflict in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md) and one fix commit, a1f34c47 'fix(dispatch): the review's five minors'. The implement handoff's fourteen proofs now stand at b5103ea3. My workspace was recreated between rounds, so the pod held neither the Postgres harness nor my client: both were rebuilt from scratch — the unpacked-Debian Postgres 17 by the recipe, and the second DPoP/RFC 8693 client written again from RFC 9449 and RFC 8693 with the Go standard library alone, never internal/broker/helper — and the whole battery was re-driven at this head against a real broker and a real Dispatch with a counting proxy between them. Everything holds: the migration applies in its new place (the live database reports version 149 with the dpop_proofs table), the three earlier findings stay closed, every acceptance line of rounds one to three repeats, and the five minors that have an observable surface are true on it. The one claim I could not drive is `callerOf` refusing a project_scope that is neither named nor person: the broker writes only those two, so that fail-closed branch is reachable from its unit test alone; both scopes it does write were driven here.
